events.title: ChatGPT launched
events.summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT to the public on November 30, 2022 — a conversational interface to GPT-3.5 that reached 100 million users faster than any prior consumer app.
events.about: ChatGPT put large language models in a chat window anyone could use: writing, coding help, tutoring, and brainstorming without API keys. It triggered an industry-wide rush into copilots, search redesigns, and enterprise AI — and changed how developers think about documentation, codegen, and UI.

narrative.whyChosen: ChatGPT was the consumer moment that made LLMs impossible to ignore.
narrative.whyImportant: It shifted software from 'AI as feature' to 'AI as interface' across every product category.
narrative.problemSolved: Powerful language models existed in research APIs but were inaccessible to non-technical users.

events.title: .NET 7 released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET 7 on November 8, 2022 with performance improvements, minimal APIs enhancements, and native AOT previews.
events.about: .NET 7 continued the annual release cadence between LTS versions: faster JSON serialization, improved cloud-native tooling, and C# 11 features like raw string literals. Teams on .NET 6 used it for bleeding-edge performance before committing to .NET 8 LTS.

narrative.whyChosen: .NET 7 kept the unified platform moving between .NET 6 and 8 LTS releases.
narrative.whyImportant: Performance and AOT work made .NET viable for CLI tools and containerized microservices.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers wanted yearly innovation without waiting for the next LTS cycle.

events.title: C# 11 released with .NET 7
events.summary: C# 11 shipped with .NET 7 on November 8, 2022 — adding raw string literals, required members, and generic math support.
events.about: C# 11's raw strings (`"""..."""`) made JSON and SQL in code readable without escape hell; `required` properties enforced initialization at compile time; static abstract interface members enabled generic math on numeric types.

narrative.whyChosen: C# 11 raw strings solved a daily pain point for config-heavy .NET apps.
narrative.whyImportant: Required members caught incomplete object initialization before runtime.
narrative.problemSolved: Multiline strings and nullable reference types needed better ergonomics together.
